subtitle: Crossing of September 2, 2026: Polymarket price in the confirmed reading of Sep 2, 8:26 PM BRT (11:26 PM UTC), presidential book at USD 141.85M, against Genial/Quaest of Sep 2 (BR-07065/2026, fieldwork Aug 30 to Sep 1, n=2,004, margin of 2pp), the only national poll released this Wednesday. Its release was already listed in the TSE registry the panel ingested on the morning of the same day. The house published TWO [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) scenarios, one with Pablo Marçal and one without, plus an unprompted scenario. ⚠️ AND THE [RUNOFF](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) AGAINST RONALDO CAIADO REVERSES THE ONE FROM THE DAY BEFORE: Quaest puts the leader ahead 42% to 37%, and Real Time Big Data of Sep 1, whose fieldwork overlaps, put Caiado ahead 45% to 43%.

candidates.name: Lula
candidates.header: PRICE: 55.50% (vol USD 9.59M accumulated), confirmed reading of Sep 2, 8:26 PM BRT (11:26 PM UTC). No change on the day, and his price has not moved off 55.50% for the fifth day running. POLLING: Genial/Quaest of Sep 2 (BR-07065/2026, fieldwork Aug 30 to Sep 1, n=2,004, margin of 2pp) puts him at 37% in both first-round scenarios and at 42% in a runoff against the runner-up, who has 41%. Against Ronaldo Caiado he wins 42% to 37%, the opposite of what the previous round measured.
fortes: He is still ahead in the first round, with 37% in both scenarios, and the distance to the runner-up is 7 points in the scenario with Marçal and 8 in the scenario without.
On price it is the fifth day running at 55.50%, and he got here without moving on any of the five.

He wins the five runoff scenarios Quaest tested: 42% to 41% against the runner-up, 42% to 37% against Ronaldo Caiado, 44% to 33% against Romeu Zema, 43% to 36% against Renan Santos and 40% to 34% against Augusto Cury.
In the runoff scenario against Caiado, Quaest puts him ahead by 5 points, while Real Time Big Data of Sep 1 put him behind by 2. The two houses measured overlapping weeks.
His rejection is 53%, two points below the runner-up's, and it is not the highest on the table.
fracos: The runoff distance against the runner-up fell to 1 point, 42% to 41%. Within Quaest itself that distance was 5pp on Aug 5 and 3pp on Aug 14, meaning it shrank in three consecutive rounds of the house.

In the first round he gave up 1 point within the house itself, from 38% on Aug 14 to 37%, and in the scenario without Marçal the distance to the runner-up widened from 7pp to 8pp through a larger fall by the opponent, not through a rise of his own.
In the second-place contract for the first round he fell 1.20pp, to 8.00%.
Government approval fell 1 point within Quaest itself, from 46% on Aug 14 to 45%, with disapproval stuck at 48% for the third round running in the house.
In the unprompted scenario, with no names shown, he has 28%, and 42% of respondents could not say whom they would vote for.
candidates.analise: Wednesday brought a single national poll, and it measures the same week as Tuesday's, shifted by one day. In the first round his picture barely changes: 37% in both scenarios, ahead. What changes is the reading of the runoff, and it changes in both directions. Against the runner-up the distance fell to 1 point, the smallest value across the three Quaest rounds. Against Ronaldo Caiado he appears ahead 42% to 37%, when the previous round, from another house, put him behind 45% to 43%. The panel does not say which of the two is right: it records that two houses measured the same week and reached opposite signs on the same pair, 7pp apart in the margin. None of that showed up on price on his side: 55.50% for the fifth day. The one that moved was the other side, which is why the distance fell from 16.55pp to 14.85pp.

candidates.name: Flávio Bolsonaro
candidates.header: PRICE: 40.65% (vol USD 9.48M accumulated), confirmed reading of Sep 2, 8:26 PM BRT (11:26 PM UTC). Up 1.70pp on the day, and the distance to the leader fell from 16.55pp to 14.85pp. POLLING: Genial/Quaest of Sep 2 (BR-07065/2026, fieldwork Aug 30 to Sep 1, n=2,004, margin of 2pp) puts him at 30% in the scenario with Pablo Marçal and at 29% in the scenario without. In the runoff he sits 1 point from the leader, 41% against 42%.
fortes: He rose 1.70pp in the winner contract, to 40.65%, and it was the only upward move among the four presidential names priced above the floor.
In the runoff he closed in: 41% against 42%, a distance of 1 point. Within Quaest itself that distance was 5pp on Aug 5 and 3pp on Aug 14.
In the second-place contract for the first round he remains dominant, at 85.50%.
The distance to the leader on price fell 1.70pp on a day when the leader did not move, meaning the compression came entirely from his side.
fracos: In the first round he gave ground within the house itself: from 31% on Aug 14 to 29% in the scenario without Marçal, and to 30% in the scenario with. The distance to the leader in the scenario without Marçal widened from 7pp to 8pp.
His rejection is 55%, the highest among the thirteen names Quaest tested, and it rose 1 point against the 54% of the house's Aug 14 round.
In the second-place contract for the first round he gave up 0.50pp, to 85.50%.
The poll shows 60% saying they do not see him as the best candidate on the right, according to G1, on the same day the third-placed name tripled.
candidates.analise: His day separates the two measurements with unusual clarity. On the declared ballot he gave ground in the first round, from 31% to 29% or 30% within the house itself, and the distance to the leader widened in the scenario without Marçal. In the runoff, which is the scenario that decides the election, he did the opposite and closed to 1 point, completing a run of three rounds by the same house in which that distance only shrank. On price the market moved in the direction of the runoff: he rose 1.70pp, to 40.65%, and since the leader stood still the distance fell to 14.85pp. The contract asks who wins the election, not who leads the first round, and this Wednesday the two pointed in different directions.

candidates.name: Renan Santos
candidates.header: PRICE: 2.20% (vol USD 12.36M accumulated), confirmed reading of Sep 2, 8:26 PM BRT (11:26 PM UTC). Down 0.35pp. In the third-place contract for the first round he fell to 28.00%. POLLING: Genial/Quaest of Sep 2 (BR-07065/2026, fieldwork Aug 30 to Sep 1, n=2,004, margin of 2pp) puts him at 3% in the first round, against 4% in the same house's round of Aug 14. In a runoff he loses to the leader 43% to 36%.
fortes: His social media accounts came back online this Wednesday, after the decision blocking his digital campaign was reversed on Sep 1, according to G1.
His rejection is 28%, the second lowest among the seven most prominent names tested, behind only Augusto Cury.
In the runoff against the leader, the 7-point margin Quaest measures is exactly the one Real Time Big Data measured the day before, and he is the only name where the two houses agree on the pair.
He filed an impeachment request against two Supreme Court justices, according to G1, and with that entered the story dominating the week's news.
fracos: On price he fell 0.35pp, to 2.20%, and lost 2.00pp in the third-place contract for the first round, where he stands at 28.00% against 52.40% for the leader of that contract.
In the first round he gave ground within the house itself, from 4% on Aug 14 to 3%, over the same span in which the third-placed name went from 2% to 10%.
His accumulated volume in the winner contract is the largest among the lower-placed names, at USD 12.36M, and even so the price is 2.20%.
He lost the lead of the third-place contract on Sep 1 and this Wednesday the distance to the leader of that contract doubled.
candidates.analise: The week began with his digital campaign blocked and unblocked in two days, and Wednesday brought the practical consequence, with his accounts back online. On the declared ballot, though, he gave ground: 3% in Quaest's first round against 4% in the same house's Aug 14 round, over the same span in which Augusto Cury went from 2% to 10%. The price followed in both contracts, down 0.35pp in the winner contract and 2.00pp in the third-place one. The only place he looks stable is the runoff against the leader, where the two houses that measured this week land on the same 7-point margin.

candidates.name: Caiado / Haddad / Zema
candidates.header: PRICE: Caiado at 0.25%, Zema at 0.15% and Haddad at 0.05% in the WINNER contract, all three below the 0.5% floor of the double reading, and this round publishes no new price for any of them in that contract. In the THIRD-PLACE contract for the first round, Caiado fell 4.50pp and stands at 8.50%, and Zema stands at 0.80%. POLLING: Genial/Quaest of Sep 2 (BR-07065/2026, fieldwork Aug 30 to Sep 1, n=2,004, margin of 2pp) gives 1% to Ronaldo Caiado and 1% to Romeu Zema in the first round. ⚠️ AND THE RUNOFF AGAINST CAIADO REVERSES THE ONE FROM THE DAY BEFORE: here the leader wins 42% to 37%.
candidates.subtitle: Back of the field in the confirmed reading of Sep 2, 8:26 PM BRT (11:26 PM UTC), and this Wednesday what changes is the reading of the back of the field itself. Ronaldo Caiado went from 4% to 1% within Quaest itself, between Aug 14 and now, and the runoff scenario in which he appeared ahead of the leader the day before, 45% to 43%, appears reversed here, with the leader ahead 42% to 37%. Two houses measuring overlapping weeks, 7pp apart in the margin of the same pair.

caiado.label: CAIADO (PSD), 0.25% (vol USD 7.05M) in the WINNER contract, below the 0.5% floor of the double reading, and this round publishes no new price for him in that contract. In the THIRD-PLACE contract for the first round, which is a different market, he fell 4.50pp and stands at 8.50% (vol USD 110 thousand). ON THIS WEDNESDAY'S DECLARED BALLOT HE LOSES THE RUNOFF TO THE LEADER, 42% TO 37%, the opposite of what the previous round measured.
caiado.fortes: His rejection is 40%, thirteen points below the leader's and fifteen below the runner-up's. He responded publicly to the 1% in the poll saying voters are still getting to know the candidates, according to O Globo, and still holds the third highest price in the third-place contract for the first round.
caiado.fracos: In the first round he fell from 4% to 1% within Quaest itself, between Aug 14 and now. In the third-place contract for the first round he lost 4.50pp in a day, to 8.50%. And the runoff scenario that put him ahead of the leader the day before puts him 5 points behind here, which shows that result did not reproduce in the next house with overlapping fieldwork.

haddad.label: HADDAD (PT), 0.05% (vol USD 7.42M) in the WINNER contract, below the 0.5% floor of the double reading, and this round publishes no new price for him. He is not a presidential candidate: he is running for governor of São Paulo.
haddad.fortes: He is not tested as a presidential candidate in the national polls of the window, so there is no ballot reading to cross against the price.
haddad.fracos: The contract remains open under his name by inheritance of the market's design, not by a declared candidacy, and the panel keeps the line only so the residual price is not read as a signal.

zema.label: ZEMA (Novo), 0.15% (vol USD 6.47M) in the WINNER contract, below the 0.5% floor of the double reading, and this round publishes no new price for him in that contract. In the THIRD-PLACE contract for the first round, which is a different market, he stands at 0.80% (vol USD 49 thousand).
zema.fortes: His rejection is 38%, the third lowest among the most prominent names Quaest tested.
zema.fracos: He has 1% in the first round, against 2% in the same house's round of Aug 14. And the runoff against the leader is the scenario where the two houses of this week disagree most: Quaest gives 44% to 33%, a margin of 11 points, and Real Time Big Data of Sep 1 gave 43% to 40%, a margin of 3. That is 8pp of difference on the same pair.

candidates.analise: The previous round had put Ronaldo Caiado ahead of the leader in a runoff, something that had not appeared in the base for any name outside the runner-up. Twenty-four hours later another house measured the same pair with overlapping fieldwork and reached the opposite sign, with the leader ahead 42% to 37%. The panel records both readings, does not choose between them, and draws attention to the size of the difference: 7pp in the margin of the pair with Caiado and 8pp in the margin of the pair with Zema, against 0pp in the pair with Renan Santos, where the two houses coincide. On price the three remain below the 0.5% floor in the winner contract, and the only publishable move is Caiado's in the third-place contract, which fell 4.50pp to 8.50%.
candidates.fortes: Rejection for the three names outside the top is lower than for the top two: Caiado 40%, Zema 38% and, among those tested, Augusto Cury at 25% against 55% for the runner-up and 53% for the leader.
candidates.fracos: None of the three reaches 2% in Quaest's first round, and the two the house tested in the runoff lose to the leader, 42% to 37% and 44% to 33%.

Down 4.50pp against the 10.85% published on Sep 1. ⚠️ IT IS THE SMALLEST BOOK ON THE PANEL: accumulated volume went from USD 86 thousand to USD 87 thousand, meaning roughly USD 1.3 thousand of fresh trading accompanies the fall of four and a half points. It is yesterday's reading in the opposite direction.

quadroComparativo.s: André Mendonça's office confirmed a meeting with Daniel Vorcaro on March 14, 2025, almost a year before he took over the case, and a statement by the businessman to the office on August 27, 2026 without the Federal Police, according to Poder360 and O Globo. The court held its first session after the report without putting the case on the agenda, according to O Globo and Folha de S.Paulo. The court's president, Edson Fachin, said justices must have limits and that he will announce the appropriate measures, and began talks with the others. Renan Santos filed an impeachment request against Moraes and Toffoli, according to G1. Mendonça's report on Moraes is expected on September 7 or 8, according to Poder360.

cruzamento: September 2 is the round in which two houses measured the same week and disagreed on who wins a runoff. On the declared ballot, Genial/Quaest of Sep 2 (BR-07065/2026, fieldwork Aug 30 to Sep 1, n=2,004, margin of 2pp) brings four things. Augusto Cury jumped from 2% to 10% within the house itself since Aug 14, and Quaest is the first poll in the base to test a runoff with him, a scenario he loses to the leader 40% to 34%. The runoff between the top two shrank to 1 point, 42% to 41%, closing three consecutive rounds of the house in which that distance only fell, from 5pp on Aug 5 to 3pp on Aug 14. In the first round, by contrast, the distance widened from 7pp to 8pp in the scenario without Marçal, through a fall by the runner-up. And the runoff scenario against Ronaldo Caiado reversed the one from the day before: here the leader wins 42% to 37%, whereas Real Time Big Data of Sep 1 put him behind 45% to 43%. That is 7pp of difference in the margin of the same pair, and in the pair against Romeu Zema the difference between the two houses is 8pp. In the pair against Renan Santos the two coincide exactly, at 7 points. The panel does not choose between the two readings: it records that the disagreement concentrates on the names outside the top and disappears where the two houses measure the same thing. On price, the leader stayed at 55.50% for the fifth day running and the runner-up rose 1.70pp, to 40.65%, so the distance fell from 16.55pp to 14.85pp, and the compression came from one side alone. Augusto Cury is the clearest case of different contracts answering different questions: in the winner contract he fell 0.75pp, to 1.60%, and in the third-place contract for the first round he rose 5.75pp, to 52.40%. The contract on a Supreme Court justice leaving through impeachment before 2027 fell from 10.85% to 6.35%, and it is worth repeating what yesterday's round already showed in the opposite direction: the book holds USD 87 thousand accumulated, the smallest on the panel, and roughly USD 1.3 thousand of fresh trading accompanies the change. A price that moves a lot on little money does not describe a change in expectations of the same size.
